messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about 0.1 atm), the freezing (melting) point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  

This is a slight depression from the standard 0 °C at 1 atm, reflecting the fact that water’s solid phase is denser than its liquid phase—so applying pressure lowers the temperature at which the two phases are in equilibrium.
